plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Gnarled, elegant branches burst into spicy-sweet, rose-pink blossoms before a single leaf appears, perfuming cool late-winter gardens and orchards with a clove-like scent.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (roughly late January through March, depending on climate)
plants.location: Japan, China and Korea, plus temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blooms weeks before cherry trees and has long been the poetic herald of spring in East Asia, where its blossoms are prized for enduring late frosts.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A towering Himalayan tree whose bare branches are crowned with enormous, goblet-shaped flowers in vivid pink, like a cloud of tulips held aloft.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to May, with early flowering in the Himalayan foothills in early March
plants.location: Himalayan foothills of Nepal, Bhutan, northeast India and southwest China
plants.funFact: A seedling can take 20 years or more to flower for the first time, so gardeners need real patience for these spectacular blooms.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: Leafless stems rise from the dry late-summer ground, each topped with a cluster of fragrant, trumpet-shaped blooms in soft blush pink.
plants.funFact: It is nicknamed the naked lady because its flowers appear after the leaves have died back, leaving the blooms standing bare on their stalks.

plants.name: Eschscholzia californica
plants.description: Silky, cup-shaped blooms in glowing orange cover hillsides and roadsides, opening in sun and folding shut on cool, cloudy days.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring, with March to May as the peak bloom period in many regions
plants.location: California and the western United States
plants.funFact: It is the official state flower of California, and its petals close at night and in cool weather.
